question.problem: Evaluate the integral ${\int }_{C}(x-y)\,\text{d}s$, where the curve $C$ is given in polar form by $r=\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }\,$ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{4}.$
question.worked_solution:
In polar coordinates, the formula for the line integral is given by

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta \,.
$$

 

The connection between polar and Cartesian coordinates gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }, \\ y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }.\end{aligned}
$$

So, along our curve, we have $x=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }$ and $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }$, where $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{4}.$

Now, if $f(x,y)=x-y$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta } \\  & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(\theta ) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}\theta }(\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }}\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta )\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta }{\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }}\end{aligned}
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  & =\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta +\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡2\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡2\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡2\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }}.\end{aligned}
$$

   

Finally, we now evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}(x-y)\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }}\cdot \text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  & =(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-(0+1) \\  & =\sqrt{2}-1\end{aligned}
$$
